glossary.systematicReview: A study that gathers every study on a question, following a fixed and transparent method.
glossary.metaAnalysis: The statistical part that combines the numbers of several studies into a single result.
glossary.outcome: An outcome is the result measured in participants, for example an intelligence score.
glossary.comparisonGroup: The groups your question compares within each study, for example operated before and after age 5.
glossary.doubleExtraction: Two people copy the numbers of each article without seeing each other's work. The system compares both versions and points out differences, which prevents typing errors.
glossary.studyVsReport: A study is a group of patients. The same group can appear in several articles; that is why articles are grouped under the study, and patients are not counted twice.
glossary.annotation: A marked passage keeps the page and the exact text of the article a number or a decision came from, so anyone can check it later.
glossary.arm: Study group (arm): a set of participants the article describes separately, for example those operated before age 5.
glossary.checks: The system distrusts typed numbers and points out what looks wrong. Fix the value or, if it is right, write a short justification: it is recorded.
glossary.agreement: Shows how often the two extractors typed the same values. Low agreement means the extraction process is worth checking.
glossary.kappa: Cohen's kappa measures agreement beyond what chance alone would give: 1 is full agreement; 0 is what luck would produce. Here it is computed only on category fields (dispersion type, final value or change, higher is better, adjusted), because it was made for categorical answers.
glossary.riskOfBias: Risk of bias is the chance that the way a study was done distorted its result. Each instrument assesses it by domains (for example, confounding or missing data), with questions that help judge each domain.
glossary.robKappa: Agreement between the two reviewers on answers and judgements. Cohen’s kappa discounts the agreement expected by chance: 1 is full agreement; 0 is what chance alone would give.
glossary.analysisPlan: Plan registered before seeing the data. Deciding after seeing the results can unintentionally lead to choosing the analysis that gives the expected answer.
glossary.adjusted: Adjusted estimate: result corrected for confounding factors (common in observational studies). Mixing adjusted and unadjusted in the same result can distort the comparison.
glossary.hartungKnapp: Adjustment that makes the confidence interval more honest when there are few studies, using the t distribution. It usually widens the interval.
glossary.i2: I²: percentage of the variation between studies that is not explained by chance.
glossary.tau2: τ² (tau²): variance of the true effect between studies.
glossary.predictionInterval: Range where a new similar study's effect would probably fall. It is wider than the CI when the studies differ.

protocol.intro: The protocol is the review plan. Define the outcomes and the groups to compare here; data extraction uses these definitions.
protocol.confirmDelete: Delete "{{name}}"? It leaves the protocol, but its history stays in the audit log.

doubleExtraction.title: Double extraction
doubleExtraction.on: On: two extractors record the numbers of each study without seeing each other's work.

outcomes.title: Outcomes
outcomes.empty: No outcomes yet. Add the main outcome of your question.
outcomes.name: Outcome name
outcomes.typeHint: Continuous: means and deviations (e.g. IQ). Dichotomous: yes/no (e.g. complication).
outcomes.timepointsHint: Separate with commas. E.g.: 12 months, 5 years

groups.title: Comparison groups
groups.empty: No groups yet. Add the two groups of your question.
groups.label: Group name
groups.ruleHint: E.g.: age at surgery below 5 years. Say what to do if a study uses another cut-off.

doubleRob.title: Double risk-of-bias assessment
doubleRob.on: On: two reviewers assess each study without seeing each other's work, and differences become conflicts.
doubleRob.off: Off: one reviewer per study. The admin still checks and submits the consensus. Report this in the Methods.

studies.intro: Each study is a group of patients. If the same group was published in several articles, they stay together in the same study.
studies.empty: No studies yet. Add or import your list.
studies.label: Study name
studies.labelHint: First author and year, e.g. Ballet 2025
studies.designHint: Used to suggest the risk of bias tool.
studies.addArticleHint: Use it when another article describes the same patients (e.g. longer follow-up).
studies.confirmDelete: Remove the study "{{label}}" and its articles from the review? Its history stays in the audit log.
studies.confirmRemoveArticle: Remove the article "{{title}}" from this study?

merge.title: Merge with another study
merge.hint: If two registered studies are actually the same patients, merge them so nobody is counted twice.
merge.confirm: The articles of "{{other}}" move to "{{study}}", and "{{other}}" leaves the list. Continue?

import.title: Import study list
import.intro: Send the spreadsheet with the studies already selected. Nothing is saved until you review and confirm.

step.mapping: Tell us which column is which

import.mappingHint: We suggested the mapping from the column names. Only the title is required; without a study name, we use the first author and year.
import.errorsIntro: Problems found: {{count}}. These rows will not be imported; fix the spreadsheet and send it again if you want.

import.missing_label: The study name is missing (or authors and year to build one).
import.invalid_year: Invalid year. Use four digits, e.g. 2021.
import.invalid_design: Design not recognized. Use, for example, Retrospective cohort or Case-control.
import.invalid_doi: Invalid DOI. It must start with 10., e.g. 10.1000/xyz.
import.duplicate_label_in_file: This study name appears more than once in the file.
import.duplicate_doi_in_file: This DOI appears more than once in the file.

study.duplicate_label: A study with this name already exists in the project.
study.duplicate_doi: An article with this DOI already exists in the project.

rob_import.unknown_study: No study in the project has this name. Register the study first or fix the name.
rob_import.duplicate_study: This study appears more than once in the file.
rob_import.other_tool: This study already uses another risk-of-bias instrument.
rob_import.already_assessed: This study already has a consensus or an import for this result; nothing was overwritten.
rob_import.missing_value: Empty cell in a required item.
rob_import.unknown_value: Value not recognised for this instrument. Use one of its levels (in Portuguese, English or as robvis writes them).

extraction_import.unknown_study: Study not linked to any study of the project. Register it or choose the match in step 3.
extraction_import.unknown_outcome: Outcome not linked to any outcome of the project.
extraction_import.unknown_timepoint: Time point not recognised. Use one of the outcome's time points in the protocol.
extraction_import.several_dispersions: The row has more than one dispersion type (e.g. SD and SE). Keep only what the article reports for this group.
extraction_import.invalid_values: Invalid combination of values in this row.
extraction_import.duplicate: This group, outcome and time point appear more than once for the same study.
extraction_import.group_conflict: The same group was linked to different comparison groups.
extraction_import.same_group: Two arms of this study were linked to the same comparison group. Combine arms with the Cochrane formula (on the study screen), not in the spreadsheet.
extraction_import.study_has_errors: This study has rows with problems (see the table below).
extraction_import.already_extracted: You already have an extraction with data for this study; nothing was overwritten.

impossible.n_not_positive: The n (or the total) must be greater than zero.
impossible.sd_not_positive: The SD must be greater than zero.
impossible.se_not_positive: The SE must be greater than zero.
impossible.negative_events: The number of events cannot be negative.
impossible.events_gt_total: The number of events cannot exceed the group total.
impossible.ci_inverted: The lower CI limit cannot be greater than the upper limit.
impossible.iqr_inverted: The 1st quartile cannot be greater than the 3rd.
impossible.range_inverted: The minimum cannot be greater than the maximum.
impossible.median_outside: The median must lie between the quartiles (or between the minimum and maximum).
impossible.ratio_not_positive: OR, RR and HR are always above zero (estimate and CI). Check the value typed.
impossible.p_out_of_range: The p value must be between 0 and 1.

textStatus.ocr: Text recognised by OCR (may contain reading errors; check the PDF)

errors.notPdf: This file is not a real PDF, even with the .pdf extension. Send the article's original PDF.
errors.failed: Could not process this PDF. Try sending it again.

search.title: Search the text
search.label: Word or passage
search.noText: This PDF has no text layer (looks scanned), so search does not work on it.

annotations.title: Marked passages
annotations.howTo: Select a passage of the article with the mouse and click "Mark passage". It becomes the source of the numbers you extract.
annotations.selectFirst: First select a passage of the PDF text.

extraction.title: Data extraction
extraction.none: Nobody has started extracting this study yet.
extraction.confirmSubmit: Submit the extraction? Once submitted, it can no longer be changed.
extraction.outdatedForm: The project form changed after you started. Check the fields; when you save, the extraction moves to the new version.
extraction.noPdf: This study has no PDF yet. Attach the article on the study page to extract with the source next to you.
extraction.noTimepoints: This outcome has no time points in the protocol. Ask the admin to add them.
extraction.addArmsFirst: Add the study groups above to record the numbers.

fields.cutoff_used: Cut-off used by the study (e.g. age at surgery)

arms.title: Study groups
arms.hint: Record every group as the article presents them (e.g. < 2, 2–5 and > 5 years) and say which protocol group each one matches. If the study has more than two groups, the system combines them, never by hand.
arms.label: Group name in the article

data.dispersionHint: Check in the article whether the number is SD or SE.
data.dispersionSource: Where the article says the type

errors.notANumber: A value is not a number. Use a comma or a dot for decimals.
errors.notAnInteger: n, events and total must be whole numbers.
errors.dispersionTypeRequired: Choose what the article reports (SD, SE, CI…) before typing the dispersion.
errors.effectIncomplete: To record the effect reported by the article, choose the measure and type the estimate.

extra.show: Other data from the article (adjusted effect, p value, t statistic)
extra.hide: Hide other data from the article
extra.hint: Use it when the article already gives the computed effect (e.g. adjusted OR with 95% CI) or only reports the p value or t statistic. Type it as in the article: the conversion to the analysis scale is done by the system.

alert.arms_exceed_total: The group sizes add up to {{sum}}, more than the study's total n ({{total}}). Check the numbers or justify (e.g. participants counted in more than one group).
alert.mean_outside_scale: The mean {{value}} is outside the scale range ({{min}} to {{max}}). Check the article.
alert.sd_too_large: The SD {{value}} is larger than half the scale range ({{half}}). That is rare: check the value and the scale.
alert.ci_excludes_mean: The 95% CI ({{low}} to {{high}}) does not contain the mean {{mean}}. A CI of the mean always contains it: check the values.
alert.dispersion_unconfirmed: Say where the article states this number is an SD, SE, CI... (e.g. footnote of Table 2). Confusing SD with SE is one of the most common errors.
alert.no_source: These numbers have no origin: enter the page/table or mark the passage in the PDF.
alert.direction_unconfirmed: Confirm the effect direction sentence for "{{outcome}}" ({{timepoint}}).
alert.effect_outside_ci: The reported effect ({{estimate}}) is outside its own CI ({{low}} to {{high}}). Check the values in the article.

direction.title: Effect direction
direction.sentence: In study {{study}}, for "{{outcome}}" ({{timepoint}}), group {{first}} had a mean of {{meanFirst}} and group {{second}} had {{meanSecond}} on the {{scale}} scale,
direction.ifWrong: If the sentence does not match the article, fix the numbers or the scale.
direction.none: The sentence appears once both protocol groups are linked to one arm each and have a mean entered.

extraction.singleNext: Extraction submitted. Since double extraction is off, the next step is to check and submit this study's consensus; only then it enters the analyses.

pending.intro: Open check alerts in the extractions you can see. Open the extraction to fix or justify them.

consensus.title: Divergences and consensus · {{study}}
consensus.intro: Here you see, field by field, what the two extractors typed. Only numbers and categories count as divergences; formatting-only differences (comma or dot, trailing zeros) do not. Each divergence needs a decision before the consensus is submitted.
consensus.waiting: Waiting for the individual extractions: {{submitted}} of {{needed}} submitted. The comparison appears once both are submitted.
consensus.single: Double extraction is off in this project: the submitted extraction already counts as the consensus and enters the analyses. To correct it later, reopen the consensus.

agreement.title: Agreement between extractors
agreement.percent: {{percent}}% of the compared values are equal ({{agreeing}} of {{items}}).
agreement.kappa: Cohen's kappa on category fields: {{kappa}} ({{items}} fields).
agreement.noKappa: Kappa could not be computed (too few category fields, or all with the same answer).
agreement.unavailable: The statistics service is down: agreement could not be computed now. The divergences below are still valid.

consensus.createHint: The consensus starts from the first extractor's values (filled in with the second's where the first left blanks). Then decide each divergence.
consensus.noDivergences: No divergences: both extractors typed the same numbers and categories.
consensus.textsHint: They do not count as divergences. Check that the consensus kept the best text and edit it if needed.
consensus.reason: Why does the consensus keep another value?

review.intro: Before locking the extraction, check every number that goes into the analysis: its value, where it came from in the article, who extracted it and how it was checked. The extraction locks only when every study has a submitted consensus and no open alert.
review.locked: The extraction is locked: no number can change. To correct something, unlock it with a justification.
review.lockHint: The button becomes available when every study is ready.
review.consensus_draft: The consensus has not been submitted yet.
review.open_alerts: {{count}} open alert(s) in the consensus: fix or justify them.
review.reopen: Reopen the consensus to correct it

check.edited: changed in the consensus, no decision recorded
check.one_extractor: recorded by one extractor only; decided by {{name}}

export.intro: Download the extracted data to use in another program or keep a copy. Numbers are exported as reported by the article, without conversions.

extraction.title: Extracted data
extraction.ready: {{ready}} of {{total}} study(ies) with a submitted consensus.
extraction.missing: {{count}} study(ies) do not have a submitted consensus yet and will be left out of the consensus file:

mode.consensus: Only the consensus (recommended). The list of what is missing goes in the "Read me" sheet.
mode.individual: Each extractor's individual extraction, marked as pre-consensus (not checked yet).

csv.excel: For Excel in Portuguese (; separator and decimal comma)
csv.r: For R or other programs (, separator and decimal point)

export.acknowledge: I am aware that {{count}} study(ies) will be left out of the file.

bibliography.title: Bibliography of the included studies
bibliography.incomplete: Authors, year or journal missing in: {{studies}}. Complete them before citing.

backup.title: Project backup
backup.intro: Creates a ZIP file with all the project data (history and removed items included) and the PDFs. Keep it off this computer; it can be restored as a new project.

formEditor.title: Study characteristics form
formEditor.help: The fields each extractor fills in about the study (country, total n, type of surgery...). Saving creates a new form version; extractions made on the old version show a warning to review. Removing a field does not delete what was already typed.
formEditor.addBack: Removed default fields (click to add them back):
formEditor.label: Field name
formEditor.optionsHint: Separate the options with semicolons (e.g. general; local; sedation)
formEditor.saveHint: Changes only apply after saving. Version {{next}} of the form will be created, and extractions already started will show a warning to review.

errors.label: Give the field a name.
errors.options: A list of options needs at least two options.

rob.intro: Choose the project's risk-of-bias instruments and set which instrument applies to each study. The system suggests and organizes; the judgement always belongs to the reviewers.

tools.title: Project instruments
tools.empty: No instrument enabled yet. An admin can enable one from the catalog below.
tools.textsFilled: Official wording pasted for {{filled}} of {{total}} questions.

catalog.title: Instrument catalog
catalog.hint: The system ships each instrument's structure (domains, number of questions and answer options), not the official wording of the questions, which is copyrighted. If the group has permission, the admin pastes the wording from the official source.
catalog.allEnabled: Every instrument in the catalog is already enabled.

scope.result: assessed per result (outcome and time point)

texts.title: Official wording of the questions
texts.hint: Paste each question exactly as in the instrument's official source, respecting its license. Without wording, the assessment screen shows only the question number and domain.
texts.question: Question {{n}}

generic.title: Domains of the generic instrument
generic.hint: Name each domain and say how many questions it has. Possible answers are Yes, Probably yes, Probably no, No, No information and Not applicable.

study.title: Risk of bias
study.noTools: The project has no risk-of-bias instruments yet.
study.suggested: Suggested by the study design: {{name}}. An admin must confirm it.
study.perResult: This instrument assesses each result separately: choose the outcome and time point.

assessment.title: Risk of bias · {{study}}
assessment.chooseVariant: Choose this domain's variant (it sets the questions):
assessment.noText: The admin has not pasted the official wording of this question yet. See the official instrument.
assessment.whyDisagree: Why do you disagree with the suggestion? (required)
assessment.noSuggestion: Answer the questions to see the suggestion.
assessment.groupRuleHint: This instrument has no official rule for the overall judgement. If the group defines one, the system suggests; without it, the judgement is free.
assessment.ready: Everything is filled in. Check and submit.

judgement.low_except_confounding: Low (except for concerns about uncontrolled confounding)

warning.several_moderate: Several domains are at moderate risk. The official guidance allows a serious overall judgement if the problems add up; the decision is yours.
warning.several_serious: Several domains are at serious risk. The official guidance allows a critical overall judgement if the problems add up; the decision is yours.
warning.several_some_concerns: Several domains raise some concerns. The manual allows a high overall judgement if this substantially lowers confidence in the result; the decision is yours.
warning.several_high: Several domains are at high risk. The official guidance allows a very high overall judgement if the problems add up; the decision is yours.
warning.no_information_needs_judgement: Information is lacking in a domain and nothing indicates serious or critical risk. The manual asks you to confirm this judgement.

missing.justificationOverall: Justify the disagreement in the overall judgement

rule.title: Group rule for the overall judgement
rule.hint: There is no official cut-off for this instrument. Set the rule your group agreed on: cases are checked in order and the first match becomes the suggestion; if none matches, the default level applies. The suggestion never replaces the reviewer’s judgement.
rule.defined: Group rule set: the system suggests the overall judgement.
rule.none: No group rule: the overall judgement is free.

agreement.title: Agreement between reviewers
agreement.summary: {{pairs}} pair(s) of assessments: {{percent}}% equal judgements ({{agreeing}} of {{items}}).
agreement.none: There are not yet two submitted assessments of the same study to compare.

consensus.title: Risk-of-bias consensus: {{study}}
consensus.intro: Both individual assessments side by side. Each conflict needs a decision: keep reviewer A’s answer, reviewer B’s, or a different value edited in the consensus and justified. Who decides is recorded.
consensus.none: No assessment has been started for this study.
consensus.waiting: Waiting for both individual assessments ({{submitted}} of 2 submitted). Until then the answers are not shown, to keep the blinding.
consensus.createHint: The consensus starts with reviewer A’s answers (filled in with B’s where A left blanks). Then decide each conflict. To keep a value different from both, edit it in the consensus and explain why here.
consensus.reason: Reason for keeping the consensus value

decided.consensus: Decided by {{name}}: value edited in the consensus.

consensus.single: Single reviewer (double assessment off): the consensus starts from their answers. Check and submit it.

table.title: Consolidated risk-of-bias table
table.intro: One table per instrument, built only from submitted consensus assessments. Instruments assessed per result show one outcome and time point at a time.
table.empty: No study has a submitted consensus for this instrument and result.
table.pending: {{count}} study(ies) are not yet in the table or the plots:

reason.in_progress: individual assessments missing (two reviewers are needed before the consensus)

plots.title: Plots (robvis)
plots.intro: Drawn by the R service with robvis, or with the same look when robvis has no template for the instrument (JBI, Newcastle-Ottawa, ROBINS-I V2, ROBINS-E). The plot’s language does not depend on the screen language.
plots.acknowledge: Draw anyway, leaving out {{count}} study(ies) without a submitted consensus

export.title: Export the table
export.intro: Uses the same language chosen for the plots. Studies without a submitted consensus are only left out with the confirmation above, and the file says which.

formats.xlsx: XLSX spreadsheet (with read-me, legend and justifications)

export.robvisHint: robvis input format (Study, D1…Dn, Overall, Weight), with the judgements in English, as robvis expects.
export.langHint: Labels follow the language chosen for the plots.

import.title: Import the group's risk-of-bias table
import.intro: For projects already under way: the group's consolidated table (robvis format or any CSV/XLSX) becomes assessments marked as imported. Each row needs a study already registered, with the same name. Nothing is overwritten: studies that already have a consensus or an import are refused.
import.mappingHint: Say which file column matches each item. Values may be in Portuguese, in English or as robvis writes them (Low, Some concerns, Serious…). Values the system does not recognise show up as errors on the row; nothing is guessed.
import.done: {{created}} assessment(s) imported. They show as imported in the table and in the exports.

review.title: Risk-of-bias review
review.intro: Before locking the stage, check where every study stands. The stage only locks with every study finished: instrument confirmed, at least one final assessment (submitted consensus or import) and nothing half done. Once locked, no answer or judgement can change.
review.locked: Risk of bias is locked: nothing can change. To fix something, unlock it with a justification.
review.lockHint: The button becomes available when every study is finished.
review.reopen: Reopen the consensus to fix it

studies.title: Studies
studies.hint: Open a study to choose the instrument and start the assessment.

plan.title: Analysis plan
plan.intro: Decide here, before seeing the results, how the meta-analysis will be done. Every analysis is compared with this plan: whatever differs shows as "not planned". Changes are kept in the audit log.
plan.notDefined: The plan has not been saved yet. The values below are the suggested defaults.

comparison.title: Comparison
comparison.hint: The effect is always group 1 versus group 2.
comparison.needGroups: Register both comparison groups above to choose the order.

cutoff.title: Cut-off
cutoff.help: Age (or another value) that separates the two groups in the review question. Each study reports the cut-off it used in the extraction form, as a number.
cutoff.strictHint: Only studies that used exactly this cut-off enter the meta-analysis.
cutoff.tolerantHint: Studies with a cut-off within the range enter; the result gets a subgroup and a sensitivity analysis by cut-off.

adjusted.title: Adjusted estimates
adjusted.label: What to do with effects adjusted for confounders

outcomes.title: Meta-analysis outcomes
outcomes.timepoint: Time point of the main analysis

sensitivity.title: Planned sensitivity analyses
sensitivity.leave_one_out: Leave one study out at a time
sensitivity.exclude_high_risk_of_bias: Without studies at high risk of bias
sensitivity.exclude_estimated_data: Without estimated data (e.g. mean from the median)

subgroups.title: Planned subgroups
subgroups.label: One per line
subgroups.hint: E.g. type of surgery, risk of bias.

checks.title: Thresholds of the plausibility alerts
checks.help: Defaults approved by the group. Alerts only warn; nothing is blocked or corrected on its own.
checks.sd_ratio: SD below this fraction of the typical
checks.se_closeness: Tolerance of SD×√n to the typical
checks.min_studies: Minimum studies on the same scale

meta.intro: The wizard guides the meta-analysis in five steps. Every calculation is done by the statistics service (metafor); the screen only shows and explains the results.
meta.noPlan: The analysis plan has not been saved yet; the wizard uses the defaults.

reason.no_consensus: The extraction of this study has no submitted consensus yet.
reason.cutoff_incompatible: The study's cut-off is not accepted by the plan's rule.
reason.cutoff_not_numeric: The study's cut-off was not entered as a number (e.g. 5).
reason.cutoff_missing: The study did not report its cut-off.
reason.no_data_for_result: There are no data for this outcome at this time point.
reason.no_comparison_in_plan: The plan does not say yet which are group 1 and group 2.
reason.missing_group: The study does not have both comparison groups mapped.
reason.missing_arm_data: Data of one of the study's groups are missing.
reason.missing_n: The number of participants of a group is missing.
reason.missing_mean: The mean (or median) of a group is missing.
reason.missing_dispersion: The dispersion (SD, SE, CI, IQR or range) is missing.
reason.missing_events: Events or total of a group are missing.
reason.mixed_value_type_in_study: One group has a final value and the other a change from baseline.
reason.no_adjusted_effect: The study has no adjusted effect for this outcome.
reason.reported_measure_differs: The effect reported by the article uses another measure.
reason.reported_effect_without_ci: The effect reported by the article has no CI.
reason.conversion_failed: The reported numbers could not be converted.
reason.combination_failed: The study's arms could not be combined.
reason.no_effect_double_zero: Zero events in both groups: the study does not enter the OR/RR.
reason.no_effect: The effect of this study could not be computed.
reason.consensus_draft: This study's consensus is a draft: open the study, check the consensus and submit it.
reason.no_extraction: This study has not been extracted yet: nobody has entered its data.

flagHelp.converted: The SD was computed from the reported SE or CI.
flagHelp.estimated: Mean and SD were estimated from the median (Wan/Luo). Consider a sensitivity analysis without this study.
flagHelp.derived: The effect was derived from the t statistic or the p value.
flagHelp.arms_combined: Several arms of the study were combined into one group (Cochrane formula).
flagHelp.reported_effect: Uses the effect already computed by the article, with its CI.
flagHelp.cutoff_tolerated: The study's cut-off differs from the question's but is within the range accepted by the plan.
flagHelp.open_alerts: The extraction still has unresolved alerts. Check the data before interpreting.
flagHelp.possible_se_as_sd: The SD is much smaller than in the other studies on the same scale and looks like a standard error. Check the article (table footnote).
flagHelp.p_inconsistent: The p value recomputed from means, SDs and n does not match the article's. There may be a typing or dispersion-type mistake.
flagHelp.influential: This study changes the result a lot (metafor's criteria). Check its data before interpreting.
flagHelp.improbable_effect: This study's effect is too large to be common. Check the data before interpreting.

block.fewer_than_two_studies: A meta-analysis needs at least 2 studies.
block.smd_mixed_final_change: The SMD cannot mix final values and changes from baseline. Use the MD or analyse them separately.
block.duplicate_study: The same study appears twice: patients would be counted twice.

measureReason.plan: It is the measure of the analysis plan.
measureReason.auto_same_scale: All studies use the same scale.
measureReason.auto_different_scales: The studies use different scales, so the effects need to be standardized.

measureHelp.MD: Difference between the group means, in the scale's unit. Use it when all studies measure with the same scale.
measureHelp.SMD: Mean difference divided by the standard deviation: allows pooling different scales (IQ, Bayley...). 0.2 is small, 0.5 medium and 0.8 large, as a general reference.
measureHelp.OR: How much the odds of the event change in group 1 versus group 2. 1 = no difference.
measureHelp.RR: How many times the risk of the event is higher (or lower) in group 1. 1 = no difference. Usually easier to explain than the OR.
measureHelp.RD: Absolute difference between the groups' risks. 0 = no difference.

step3.title: Direction
step3.intro: Check each study's scale. Where "higher is worse", the statistics service inverts the sign of the effect, so all of them point the same way in the plot.

step4.title: Model
step4.intro: The default comes from the analysis plan. Changing it here is allowed, but the analysis is marked "not planned".

methodHelp.REML: Random effects: assumes the true effect varies from study to study. REML is the recommended estimator.
methodHelp.DL: Random effects with the classic DerSimonian-Laird estimator. It may underestimate the variation with few studies.
methodHelp.PM: Random effects with the Paule-Mandel estimator.
methodHelp.FE: Fixed effect: assumes every study measures the same true effect. Rare in observational studies.

meta.notPlanned: Not planned analysis: differs from the plan in

summary.favours: Considering {{k}} study(ies), for the outcome {{outcome}} ({{timepoint}}), the result favoured {{favoured}}: {{measure}} = {{effect}}.
summary.none: Considering {{k}} study(ies), for the outcome {{outcome}} ({{timepoint}}), there was no clear difference between {{group1}} and {{group2}}: {{measure}} = {{effect}}. The 95% CI includes the value of no difference.
summary.prediction: A new similar study would probably have an effect between {{lb}} and {{ub}} (prediction interval).

warning.few_studies: Fewer than 5 studies: heterogeneity estimates (I², τ²) are unstable.
warning.few_studies_heterogeneity_unstable: Fewer than 5 studies: heterogeneity estimates are unstable.
warning.estimated_data: There are estimated data (mean from the median). Consider a sensitivity analysis without them.
warning.studies_with_open_alerts: Some studies have unresolved extraction alerts. Check the data before interpreting.
warning.direction_inverted: The sign of some studies was inverted because their scale is "higher is worse".
warning.mixed_final_change: Some studies report final values and others changes from baseline (allowed with the MD).
warning.double_zero_excluded: Studies with zero events in both groups were left out of the OR/RR.
warning.continuity_correction_applied: A continuity correction (0.5) was applied to studies with zero events in one group.
warning.knha_not_for_fixed_effect: The Hartung-Knapp adjustment does not apply to a fixed effect.
warning.plausibility_alerts: There are plausibility alerts (possible SE instead of SD or a p value that does not match). Check the studies marked in step 1.
warning.influential_studies: There are influential studies: the result changes a lot without them. Check their data before interpreting.
warning.improbable_effects: Some studies have an improbable effect. Check the data before interpreting.
warning.influence_needs_three_studies: With fewer than 3 studies the influence of each one cannot be assessed.

forest.title: Forest plot
forest.robHelp: Shows, beside each study, the domains and the overall risk-of-bias judgement of the chosen tool (the final assessment: consensus or imported). Studies without a final assessment show empty cells.

howToRead.title: How to read this plot
howToRead.square: Each row is a study. The square is that study's effect.
howToRead.line: The horizontal line is the study's 95% confidence interval: the shorter, the more precise the study.
howToRead.null: The vertical dotted line marks "no difference" (0 for MD/SMD, 1 for OR/RR). An interval crossing it shows no clear difference.
howToRead.diamond: The diamond at the bottom is the pooled effect: its centre is the estimate and its tips the 95% CI.
howToRead.prediction: The dotted line around the diamond is the prediction interval: where a new study's effect would probably fall.
howToRead.weights: The size of the square and the percentage show each study's weight in the result.
howToRead.marks: Studies with *, † or ‡ have estimated, converted or derived data (see the note under the plot).

check.possible_se_as_sd: {{arm}}: the SD ({{sd}}, n = {{n}}) is much smaller than the typical SD of this scale ({{typical}}), and SD×√n = {{times}} is close to it. This value may be an SE. Check the article.
check.p_inconsistent: The article reports p = {{reported}}, but with the typed means, SDs and n the p would be {{recomputed}}. Check the numbers and the dispersion type.

history.title: Analysis history
history.help: Each saved analysis keeps the exact data, the settings, the result and the R versions. If a consensus value changes later it shows as outdated; run it again to update.
history.confirmRemove: Remove this analysis from the history? It stays stored in the database and the audit log.

reason.data_changed: A number of a study in this analysis was corrected after it was saved.
reason.studies_changed: A study gained or lost its consensus after it was saved: the studies that enter may have changed.

sens.title: Sensitivity analyses
sens.help: They redo the analysis changing one thing at a time, to see whether the conclusion holds. Those marked "planned" are in the analysis plan.
sens.notPlanned: This sensitivity analysis is not in the analysis plan: report it as not planned.

label.without_high_risk: Without studies at high risk of bias

warning.studies_without_risk_of_bias: Some studies have no final risk-of-bias assessment for this result yet and were left out of this analysis.
warning.leave_one_out_needs_three_studies: Leaving one study out needs at least 3 studies.

sub.title: Subgroups
sub.help: Analyses separately by a characteristic of the studies and tests whether the effect differs between subgroups. With few studies per subgroup the test has little power: interpret with caution.
sub.notPlanned: This subgroup is not in the analysis plan: report it as a not planned analysis.
sub.test: Test for subgroup differences: Q = {{q}}, df = {{df}}, p = {{p}}.
sub.testHelp: Compares the subgroup effects. A small p suggests the effect changes with the characteristic, but does not prove cause: studies may differ in other ways.
sub.leftOut: No information for this characteristic (left out): {{studies}}.

warning.subgroup_with_one_study: A subgroup has a single study: its value is only that study's effect.
warning.subgroup_with_few_studies: A subgroup has fewer than 3 studies: the estimate is unstable.

pb.title: Publication bias
pb.help: Small studies with 'negative' results are sometimes not published. The funnel plot and Egger's test look for that sign, but other things (such as heterogeneity) produce the same shape.
pb.few: With fewer than 10 studies, the funnel plot and Egger's test have little power and cannot support a conclusion. Do not claim there is or there is not publication bias based on them.
pb.eggerHelp: Tests whether small studies show different effects from large ones. A small p suggests asymmetry, which may be publication bias or another cause; a large p does not prove there is no bias.
pb.funnelHelp: Each dot is a study: the effect on the horizontal axis and the standard error on the vertical one (larger studies at the top). Without bias, the dots spread symmetrically inside the funnel.

nar.title: Narrative synthesis
nar.help: Studies that could not enter the meta-analysis of this outcome are still part of the review. Read each one and record which way its result points; the system does not decide this.
nar.empty: Every study with data entered the meta-analysis: there is nothing for the narrative synthesis.
nar.missing: {{n}} study(ies) out of the meta-analysis still without a recorded direction.
nar.note: Note (e.g. where it is in the article)

mr.title: Meta-regression
mr.help: Tests whether a characteristic of the studies (e.g. mean age at surgery) explains part of the difference between results. With few studies the result is unstable: use it to explore, not to conclude.
mr.few: There are fewer than 10 studies per moderator, as the Cochrane Handbook recommends. The result is unstable and must not be read as a conclusion.
mr.logScale: For RR and OR, the coefficients are on the log scale (as metafor returns them).
mr.leftOut: Left out because the moderator is missing: {{studies}}.

ml.title: Several time points together (multilevel model)
ml.help: When the same study reports the outcome at several time points, the results are not independent. The multilevel model uses every time point and treats the study as a cluster, without counting the same study twice.
ml.few: Fewer than 5 studies: the between- and within-study variances are unstable.

searches.title: Searches
searches.intro: Import here the file exported from each database (PubMed, LILACS, Embase...). Record the date and the search strategy: they go into the PRISMA flow diagram and the Methods. Nothing is removed at this step: duplicates are handled later, always with confirmation.
searches.strategyHint: Paste the strategy exactly as it was run in the database.
searches.formats: Accepted formats: RIS (.ris), PubMed/MEDLINE (.nbib or .txt), BibTeX (.bib) and CSV. Up to 100 MB.
searches.total: {{count}} reference(s) imported in total, before removing duplicates.
searches.reportCut: The report shows the first 200 problems.
searches.confirmRemove: Remove the {{database}} search and its references? Nothing is erased for good: it stays in the history.

dedup.title: Duplicates
dedup.help: The same reference often appears in more than one database. Removing duplicates avoids screening the same article twice, and the number removed goes into the PRISMA flow diagram.
dedup.intro: The system only points out the pairs and explains why. You decide which record stays; the other leaves the screening, but nothing is erased and every decision can be undone.
dedup.summary: {{imported}} reference(s) imported; {{removed}} duplicate(s) removed; {{left}} go to screening.
dedup.confirmCertain: Confirm the {{count}} certain ones (same DOI or PMID)
dedup.confirmCertainAsk: Confirm every pair with the same DOI or PMID? In each pair the record imported first stays. They can be undone one by one.
dedup.thresholdHelp: From 0.80 to 1. The approved default is 0.95: only nearly identical titles become probable duplicates. Lower finds more pairs, with more false positives to check.

kindHelp.certain: Same DOI or same PMID: it is the same article.
kindHelp.probable: Nearly identical title, same year, same first author and same journal, volume and pages when both have them. Check side by side.
kindHelp.related: Alike, but different in numbers or in words such as Part, Erratum, Comment or Retraction. Never duplicates: shown because an erratum may matter.

criterion.yearMissing: one of them has no year

screening.title: Title and abstract screening
screening.help: Read the title and abstract and decide whether the study may be relevant. Two reviewers decide without seeing each other; when they disagree, the admin resolves.
screening.intro: When in doubt, choose Maybe: the article goes on to be checked and nothing is lost. Confirmed duplicates do not appear here.
screening.overall: in the project: {{include}} included, {{exclude}} excluded, {{conflict}} in conflict, {{pending}} waiting for the second reviewer
screening.blindOn: Blind screening is on: you only see your own decisions until the admin reveals them.
screening.usefulHelp: Mark studies that do not enter the review but are worth citing in the Introduction or Discussion.
screening.shortcuts: Shortcuts: I include · E exclude · T maybe (or 1, 2, 3) · U undo · ← → move.

emptyView.todo: Nothing for you to decide now. Check that searches were imported and duplicates resolved.
emptyView.done: You have not decided any reference yet.

admin.title: Admin tools
admin.kwHint: Separate with semicolons or lines. They only highlight the text: they decide nothing.
admin.blindHelp: With blind screening each reviewer sees only their own decisions, also through the API. Turn it off only when the reviewers have finished.
admin.revealAsk: Turn blind screening off? Reviewers will see each other's decisions.
admin.batchesHelp: Share out the references: each reference goes to up to two reviewers, and only they decide on it. Without batches any reviewer can screen everything.
admin.kappaHelp: Cohen's kappa measures how much reviewers agree beyond what chance would explain. It goes from -1 to 1: near 1 is almost full agreement; near 0, the same as chance. Computed by the statistics service (R).
admin.noAgreement: No reference has been decided by both reviewers yet.

screening.fullTextIntro: Only articles included at title and abstract come here. Read the full text (attach the PDF to the study if needed) and decide: Include or Exclude, always with the reason.
screening.reasonHint: Required to exclude. Reasons appear in the PRISMA flow diagram.

reasons.title: Exclusion reasons
reasons.help: The list belongs to the project. Unused reasons can be removed; used ones can be renamed or merged into another (their decisions move to the other reason). Everything stays in the history.
reasons.mergeAsk: Merge "{{from}}" into "{{to}}"? Its decisions move to "{{to}}". The change stays in the history.

included.title: Included articles not yet a study
included.help: Each included article becomes a new study or joins an existing study as one more report (the same cohort published in another article). This way the same patients are not counted twice.
included.label: Study name (e.g. Silva 2020)

priority.help: A simple machine learning model (no generative AI, it runs on the server) learns from the decisions already made and puts first the references most similar to the included ones. It only changes the order: it never excludes or decides anything.
priority.info: Model trained on {{includes}} included/maybe and {{excludes}} excluded; {{scored}} reference(s) ordered.
priority.warning: Priority order helps find relevant studies sooner, but every reference still needs to be read, unless the protocol defines a stopping rule.
priority.needs: Ordering is not possible yet: decide at least {{min}} included (or maybe) and {{min}} excluded. Now: {{includes}} and {{excludes}}.

prisma.title: PRISMA 2020 flow diagram
prisma.help: PRISMA is the guideline for reporting a systematic review. The flow diagram shows how many records came in, how many left at each step and why.
prisma.intro: The numbers come from the system itself: searches, duplicates, screening, full text, studies and saved analyses. If the group imported only the final list, adjust the counts by hand, always with a justification.

warning.title_abstract_pending: Some references are still waiting for a decision or in conflict at title and abstract screening.
warning.full_text_pending: Some articles are still waiting for a decision or in conflict at full text.
warning.screened_does_not_add_up: Identified minus duplicates does not match the number screened. Check the adjusted counts.
warning.sought_does_not_add_up: Screened minus excluded does not match the number of reports sought.
warning.assessed_does_not_add_up: Sought minus not retrieved does not match the number assessed.

checklist.title: PRISMA 2020 checklist
checklist.help: The 27 items PRISMA asks to report in the article. For each one, mark whether the manuscript reports it and where (section and page). The system says when it already has data for the item, but the group marks it.
checklist.source: The item summaries were written by RevisaMeta. Read the official wording at
checklist.hasData: the system has data for this item

grade.title: Certainty of evidence (GRADE)
grade.help: GRADE rates how much we can trust the result of each outcome: high, moderate, low or very low.
grade.intro: Choose the outcome and timepoint. The system runs the same analysis as the meta-analysis screen and suggests, for each domain, whether certainty should go down or up. The group decides, always with a justification.

approachName.classic: Classic GRADE (observational studies start at low)

grade.startObservational: There are observational studies: in classic GRADE certainty starts at low.
grade.startRandomized: Only randomized trials: certainty starts at high.

domainHelp.risk_of_bias: Rate down when many studies are at high risk of bias.
domainHelp.inconsistency: Rate down when study results differ a lot (high I²).
domainHelp.indirectness: Rate down when studies do not answer exactly the question (e.g. another age cutoff).
domainHelp.imprecision: Rate down when the confidence interval is wide and includes no effect.
domainHelp.publication_bias: Rate down when there are signs that negative studies were not published.
domainHelp.large_effect: For observational studies, rate up when the effect is very large.
domainHelp.dose_response: Rate up when more exposure leads to more effect. Only the group judges it.
domainHelp.plausible_confounding: Rate up when likely confounding would reduce the observed effect. Only the group judges it.

reason.rob_no_tool: Choose a tool to see the suggestion.
reason.rob_ok: Few studies at high risk ({{high}} of {{k}}).
reason.imprecision_ok: The 95% CI does not include no effect.
reason.publication_bias_few: Only {{k}} studies; Egger needs at least {{min}}.
reason.large_effect: Large RR/OR and no downgrade suggested.
reason.large_effect_no: Effect is not large or a downgrade was suggested.

kind.deadline: The project deadline ends in {{days}} day(s) ({{deadline}}).
kind.archived: Project archived for inactivity (last change on {{last_activity}}). Nothing was deleted.
kind.ai_disabled: An AI feature was switched off: {{accuracy}}% accuracy, below the {{threshold}}% threshold.

ai.title: Artificial intelligence (optional)
ai.help: The AI only explains and points at PDF passages. It never computes statistics, never decides inclusion or risk of bias, and nothing it suggests becomes data without a person's confirmation.
ai.on: The AI is on in this project.
ai.off: The AI is off in this project.
ai.notConfigured: This server has no AI provider configured yet. Even if turned on, the AI stays unavailable until the server owner adds the key.
ai.newNotice: The data-use notice changed. The AI stays off until an admin reads and accepts the new version.
ai.lowAccuracy: The "{{fn}}" feature was switched off automatically because its accuracy fell below the threshold. An admin can turn it back on.

fn.tutor: Tutor: explains concepts and the project's results
fn.extract: Assisted extraction: points at values printed in the PDF

ai.adminOnly: Only a project admin can turn the AI on or off.

metrics.title: AI accuracy in this project
metrics.intro: How many AI suggestions people found correct, among the latest reviewed. Below the threshold, the feature is switched off automatically.

tutor.title: Tutor
tutor.intro: Ask what a result or a concept means. The tutor only explains: numbers come from the computation done by R, and it decides nothing for you.
tutor.question: Your question
tutor.unverified: Warning: these numbers did not come from the computation and were not verified: {{items}}. Do not use them without checking.
tutor.source: AI-generated answer ({{provider}}, {{model}}, prompt {{version}}). Check before using.

locate.title: Find passage
locate.intro: Ask where the article talks about something (e.g. "blinding of assessors"). The AI points at the page and the exact passage; the system checks the passage exists in the PDF. Read the page and decide yourself.
locate.question: What are you looking for?
locate.discarded: {{n}} suggested passage(s) were not in the PDF text and were discarded.
locate.none: No checked passage was found. Try other words or use the search above.

assist.discarded: {{n}} suggestion(s) discarded: the passage is not in the PDF or the number is not in the passage.

extract.title: Suggest values to extract
extract.intro: The AI points at numbers printed in the article, each with its passage and page, checked by the system. It never fills the form: check the page and type the value yourself.
extract.request: What to extract (e.g. mean and SD of IQ in the < 5 years group)

rob.title: Risk of bias second opinion
rob.intro: Paste the signalling question. The AI suggests an answer with the passage that supports it, checked in the PDF. The judgement is yours.
rob.question: Signalling question
rob.discarded: The suggestion was discarded: the quoted passage is not in the PDF or the answer is not one of the options.

search.title: Search strategy help
search.intro: From the protocol question and PICO, the AI suggests MeSH and DeCS descriptors, synonyms and a PubMed query. Review carefully (ideally with a librarian) before running it.
search.review: Check that each descriptor exists in MeSH/DeCS and adjust before use. The system does not run the search.

draft.title: Draft of Methods and Results
draft.intro: The AI writes a draft; numbers are inserted by the system (PRISMA counts). Bracketed notes are reminders for the group to complete.
draft.edit: Copy into the manuscript and edit. The text is a starting point, not a final version.

digitizer.title: Graph digitizer
digitizer.intro: Use it when the article only shows the number in a graph. The image stays in your browser and is not uploaded. Click two known points on each axis and type their values; then click the data points. When you use a value, set its source to "read from a graph".
digitizer.pick: Choose the graph image (screenshot of the figure)

step.x1: Click the first known point on the X axis
step.x2: Click the second known point on the X axis
step.y1: Click the first known point on the Y axis
step.y2: Click the second known point on the Y axis

error.values: Type the values of the four calibration points.
error.axes: The two points of each axis need different values (and positive ones on a log axis).

digitizer.approximate: Values read from a graph are approximate. Prefer the number in the text or a table when there is one, and consider a sensitivity analysis without these data.

writing.title: Congress abstract
writing.intro: Create a structured draft with the system's numbers (no AI). The conclusion and the final text are always the group's. The counters show whether the text fits the congress limits.

profile.title: My profile
profile.twoFactorHelp: Besides the password, login asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app (e.g. Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or Aegis).
profile.secret: Key to type in the app:
profile.codes: Keep these recovery codes somewhere safe. Each works once, in case you lose your phone. They will not be shown again.
profile.disableHelp: To turn it off, type your password and a code from the app (or a recovery code).

extractionImport.title: Import an extraction spreadsheet
extractionImport.intro: Bring the numbers of a spreadsheet the group already filled in. Each study becomes your draft extraction, with every check of the form (dispersion type, impossible values, direction sentence, double extraction and consensus). Nothing is saved until you check and confirm.
extractionImport.layoutTitle: How the spreadsheet must be laid out
extractionImport.layout: One row per study, group, outcome and time point, with the numbers of that group. Studies, comparison groups and outcomes must exist in the project (names may differ: you link each one in step 3). Use one column per dispersion type (SD, SE, CI, quartiles or minimum and maximum); the type comes from the filled column, and each row may have only one.
extractionImport.layoutNote: FICTITIOUS example. Comma or dot decimals are accepted, in CSV or XLSX.
extractionImport.mappingHint: We suggested the matches from the column names. Study, group and outcome are required.

step.names: Link the spreadsheet names to the project

extractionImport.namesHint: Names equal to the project's are already linked. Choose the ones left without a match here. A group without a match becomes an arm of the study with no comparison group; you can link it later in the extraction.
extractionImport.errorsIntro: Problems found: {{count}}. A study with any problem row is not imported (never half); fix the spreadsheet and send it again.
extractionImport.next: Next step: open each study, check the numbers against the article (each value's source and the alerts are shown there) and submit the extraction.

fields.source_location: Where it is in the article
fields.dispersion_source: Where the article states the dispersion type

dashboard.noDeadline: No deadline set. You can add one in the project details.
dashboard.allDone: Every stage tracked here is done.
dashboard.peopleHint: Counts only: nobody sees other people's decisions or answers here.

count.protocol: {{done}} of {{total}} items: at least one outcome and two comparison groups.
count.extraction: {{done}} of {{total}} studies with a submitted consensus.
count.rob: {{done}} of {{total}} studies with a final assessment.
count.analysis: {{done}} of {{total}} outcomes with a saved meta-analysis.
count.grade: {{done}} of {{total}} outcomes with certainty of evidence assessed.

next.protocol: Add the outcomes and the two groups to compare. They organise extraction and analysis.
next.screening: Finish screening the imported references and resolve the conflicts.
next.extraction: Extract each study's numbers, check the alerts and submit the consensus.
next.rob: Choose each study's instrument and assess its risk of bias.
next.analysis: Run and save the meta-analysis of each outcome.
next.grade: Assess the certainty of evidence (GRADE) of each outcome.
